text: And in the even longer term, the health of the population, in terms of prevalence of chronic diseases, mortality rate for cancer, for example.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the range of key performance indicators (KPIs) runs into hundred and beyond, but we will continue to monitor all of them.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first is for Senior Minister of State Koh.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It was mentioned that there was a Masters in audiology.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But my question is whether we have plans for a diploma or undergraduate in audiology, as well as podiatry, which I understand we do not have any localised courses as stated on the NUHS website.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Tan on flexible work arrangements for supporting caregivers.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I understand that flexible work arrangements are differing context to context and workplace to workplace.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can MOH help to formalise the caregiver status and legitimise their need for flexibility in a way that they can better demonstrate to their employer the need for that flexibility?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The third question is on the Integrated Community Care Provider arrangements.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would there be enhancements in the pipeline beyond clinical outcomes to also having access one financial assessments, as well as a one employment coordinator for seniors who might be looking for part time employment?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We do see the need for social prescription in combating loneliness, which, as Senior Minister of Tan had highlighted, is equivalent of smoking 15 cigarettes a day.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question is, as we measure medical prescriptions, how are social prescriptions therefore measured and interventions tracked?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question also stems from how AAC participation is the current measure from a previous Parliamentary Question that I filed regarding attendance as well as participation.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can we better take into account other areas that the seniors might be active in, for example, in faith-based or Community Club or Centre events or course-based initiatives that they might be volunteering at?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Senior Minister of State Tan also highlighted there were studies ongoing with schools and if he could share a bit more details about what that entails?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But there are actually some of these audiology programmes that are done at a lower level.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, I do believe that there are some basic industrial audiometry course at Temasek Polytechnic, but that is really more for industrial application of technicians who are actually screening at the industry level, not so much as a clinical setting where you actually provide services at the hospital.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I will answer the last question and for the first two questions, Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How will answer.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are there to provide the support, the funding, to make it as easy as you can come to the AAC to participate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as to what you do with your life, I am afraid I cannot track it and I do not think I should track it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But please enrol for Healthy 365 – at least, the app will help you track.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To Mr Cai, please correct me if I heard your questions wrongly, because I was trying to get all your four questions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, diet, lifestyle, exercise and many more other areas.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, certainly, that should be part of that care plan, but this goes beyond what the Integrated Community Care Provider does, which focuses more on seniors and the needs of those seniors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In each area, each sub-region, there are different providers, different parties providing different services – from befriending services, rehabilitation services and many more.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, bringing the different partners together, having a common language in which to discuss, understand and reach out and provide services to a senior is non-trivial.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Having a standardised tool based on this assessment, developing a care plan, implementing this care plan and getting our seniors to go through the care plan entirely is non-trivial.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, I would say, let us take one step at a time and there are already many activities and other partners in the community providing different services and volunteering opportunities for seniors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is really part of the fabric of a diverse community and very much part of the "we first" society.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, I have a clarification for Minister of State Tan Kiat How.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: I would like him to confirm whether MOH will take up my suggestion of a caregiver passport and whether MOH has any considerations which may prevent the suggestion from being adopted.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I mentioned in my speech the different Ministries' efforts to support caregivers, and we understand the challenges that caregivers face, juggling between work and care.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is something they are working on, including flexible work arrangements and other initiatives.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will continue to work with our colleagues and other partners in the community.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And Mr Fadli Fawzi's question around the caregiver passport, if I get it correctly, that he has referenced in his cut, from the UK.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As I mentioned in my speech earlier, I think Mr Fawzi was not in the room, we certainly welcome all suggestions from Members, including suggestions that other Members have raised as part of this MOH COS and in other occasions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Specifically to his suggestion, I looked at it online.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, some hospitals may provide longer visiting times.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The hospital canteen may give some discounts to caregivers eating there and some supermarkets might give some discounts too.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is a ground-up initiative, where different parties come in.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Because it is a ground-up initiative, I understand that the implementation can be quite uneven.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Caregivers going to different parts of the city in the UK may have different experiences.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Going to different supermarkets will have different experiences.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Some supermarkets do provide the support, some do not.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And like many ground-up initiatives, we certainly welcome them.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And there are many funding schemes in Government to support ground-up initiatives.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If Mr Fadli Fawzi knows of individuals or parties who want to support our caregivers and organise a ground-up effort, we will look at those proposals.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Three clarifications for Senior Minister of State Koh.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Senior Minister of State had shared earlier about the NMHO that was established to coordinate multi-agency initiatives.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And how often will this, if any, be reported?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Senior Minister of State also mentioned that tied care and a no-wrong door approach, which I welcome.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Will MOH share the desired service standards, for example, maximum time to first contact, maximum time to first clinical appointment for moderate or high risk cases and escalation protocols across settings?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And my third and final one is Senior Minister of State spoke about retention measures for nurses and allied health staff.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And in terms of KPIs, therefore, the First Stops would not have waiting time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There are counsellors who are manning the phone lines that you can actually call anytime to speak to them or to text them on WhatsApp.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I think from that first touchpoint, there is really no waiting time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But what is important is to make sure that the individual who gets into the first touchpoint, is prepared to also receive help from higher tiers of care if they need to.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Often time, this is where the challenge is.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Many of them will be reluctant to move on to the next tier of care, because as all of us have dealt with in a community on challenging individuals with mental health issues, sometimes getting them to even come forward to seek help is the problem.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is not that the resources are not there, but they are not willing to come forward.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is difficult, so it is really about convincing them, working with them, earning their trust.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And we hope that some of the First Stop resources we put forth will be a way in which our counsellors can convince the individual through a phone call to be prepared to step forward and receive care.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Having said that, that will flow into the second question on the Tiered Care Model, on whether there are ways to monitor those who are at high risk and whether they receive care.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Again and following from the train of thought, I would want to assure the Member that those who are deemed to be high risk will always be prioritised.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Like I said, the biggest hurdle is whether they are prepared to step forward and not really the care capacity per se.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I hope this is something that the Member can understand, why it is not meaningful for us to track some of these timelines, because the counterfactual is unmeasurable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There is no way to measure who are at risk and whether they turn up or eventually they become a suicide case.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we will therefore, focus on putting forth resources, to make sure that if they are prepared to step forward, the resources will be available.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the third question on retention for psychologists.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: At the moment, we are not looking at anything more than that for now.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But let us take it one step at a time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Certainly, in the healthcare sector, we also have given out retention and measures to AHPs, I think it was in just about 2025, if I am not wrong.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we will look at it holistically as part of supporting our AHPs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And this is based on feedback that I have received from residents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, if I may frame my question posed in my cut another way: what does the Minister perceive might be the logistical or behavioural difficulties that is associated with allowing this sort of limited carry-over of annual MediSave limits?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am not going to immediately say "Yes, good idea", or "No, we will reject it".

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My clarification is on ageing and the super-aged society.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Of the seniors living within the vicinity of the AACs, what proportion of them are actually actively engaged?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And secondly, I understand that offices, like the SGO, do proactively engage seniors in their premises, but what else are we doing differently to engage seniors who are socially isolated who may not voluntarily step forward to join the AAC activities?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: First, it is not just the number of the AACs; which is one thing.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The number of AACs make it more convenient, easier for seniors to come by to an AAC near their home and in an environment they are familiar with, in a neighbourhood they are familiar with.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That is why we have expanded the footprint.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But beyond the number of AACs, it is also the activities that the AACs do to make it meaningful for the seniors, so that they come by and they are not socially isolated.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They come by, they participate, they are engaged, they make new friends.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And hopefully, they also can make changes to their lifestyle so that they can be healthier and happier.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And in the coming years, we will do more to expand the number of activities that AACs do, going beyond maybe just doing, for example, activities like healthy rumba and so on, to also create more awareness about health and also having CHPs within the AACs to provide services to our seniors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And we will continue to explore how we can do more.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So that it is not just quantity, but the kind of activities.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Thirdly, at the SGO, we have Silver Generation Ambassadors who reach out to seniors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They do so not just to reach out and speak to the seniors – they do befriending as well as preventive health visits – understanding the circumstances of the seniors that they visit at home, what kind of needs the seniors have, what kind of family circumstances are behind the closed door, and identify services, especially those near the seniors' homes, that are relevant to them and connect them to those services – whether it is AACs, SCCs or even mental health services.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Silver Generation Ambassadors go beyond just doing visitations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They also provide a valuable touchpoint to the community and a connector to services that are around the vicinity of the senior.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will want to do more for seniors who are socially isolated.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have been working with community partners, not just AACs and SCCs, but also other organisations in the community, including faith-based organisations and voluntary organisations to reach out to those seniors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: ICCP will work out the assessment and care plan for those seniors and crowd in partners to reach out to those seniors, especially those who live by themselves.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, to the Member's point, I welcome any suggestions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is an important priority for MOH in the coming years.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I should clarify that I do not usually watch his TikTok videos, but that particular one was referred to me.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I heard feedback from some people in the insurance industry that that video on IPs and riders created an impression in some members of the public that riders were not really necessary.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In the video, riders were symbolised by a wooden horse.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I think at one point in time, the Minister flicked the horse off the table.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I do not know whether the Minister is aware of that feedback that that video may have given the impression to members of the public that riders are not really that useful.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could he take this opportunity to reaffirm again that riders are indeed prudent for the reasons that I have mentioned in my cut?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is a challenge when attention span is so short and you try to put so much information in a short video.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am not surprised the insurance industry gave you that feedback, but I think the video and the information that we have been putting out is a serious one, which is you have to examine if you really need a rider.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The purpose of insurance is to cover expenses that we cannot afford.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For most of us, it is because if we have a big inpatient episode running into tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands of dollars, a big bill, the insurance plus subsidy can cover it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We put cancer aside, the rider covers co-payment.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is the core purpose of the rider.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Given your premium, as you get older, the rider premium goes up the most, balance the cost and benefit to see if a rider is suitable for you.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the core message of the video continues to be accurate, that we should really take a look at our financial needs, what risks are we trying to protect and examine – do I need a rider?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some really wish to pay more premium in order to cover as much as you can.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But for others, especially those who use public health institutions, use subsidised care, take a close look if you really need the rider.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: To follow up with the Minister, is it not the case that if you do not have a rider, there is an exposure that the patient will have to pay hospitalisation bills at 10% without any cap?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: That is one of the concerns about loss limits in that sense.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Then, consider whether a rider is suitable for you.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Remember, that in a public health institution, when you cannot afford it, there is MediFund that you can always apply for.

speaker: The Chairman
text: On that note, I think all clarifications have been asked and responded to.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Can I invite Ms Mariam Jaafar, if you would like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: I think healthcare is probably one of the most complex Ministries.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: On behalf of this Health Government Parliamentary Committee, I would like to say thank you to the healthcare family, from everyone at MOH to the frontliners in the hospitals and community.
